title: Accounts Assistant
description:
I'm currently recruiting for an Accounts Assistant on behalf of a well-established professional services business based in Sunderland.

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to build their career in finance, with structured training, professional qualifications and genuine progression opportunities.

The Role
Working closely with the finance team, you'll support the day-to-day running of the accounts function, including:
- Processing supplier invoices, payments and expenses.
- Managing customer receipts and assisting with credit control.
- Completing bank reconciliations and maintaining accurate records.
- Supporting billing queries and resolving discrepancies.
- Assisting with VAT coding and financial reporting.
- Maintaining financial records and supporting compliance procedures.

About You
We're looking for someone who is organised, numerate and has excellent attention to detail.
You'll ideally have:
- Experience in an accounts or finance administration role (desirable).
- Good Microsoft Excel and general accounting software skills.
- Strong communication and organisational skills.
- The ability to manage deadlines and work independently or as part of a team.
- A genuine interest in developing a long-term career in finance.

AAT qualification or studying towards AAT would be beneficial, but practical experience and a willingness to learn are equally welcomed.
What's On Offer?
- Salary dependent on experience.
- Full-time hours: Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm.
- 27 days annual leave plus Christmas Eve.
- Pension and health benefits.
- Life insurance (subject to eligibility).
- Employee support programme.
- Ongoing training and development.
- Support towards AAT Level 4 and further qualifications.
- Clear opportunities for career progression.
- Regular team socials and discounted services.

Location: Sunderland - office-based.
If you're looking to take the next step in your finance career and want to join a supportive team that invests in your development, I'd love to hear from you.
Please get in touch to discuss the opportunity in confidence.

title: Emergency Works Scheduler
description:
Salary from £29,286 + Up to 5% Bonus
Permanent, 40 Hours Per Week
Based at Doxford Park, Sunderland

Keeping communities safe, one call at a time

Join our dynamic Dispatch Team at Northern Gas Networks (NGN) as an Emergency Works Scheduler. This role is central to our operations, acting as the key contact between our customers and field-based Gas Operatives. You will be responsible for scheduling and dispatching both emergency and non-emergency work, ensuring safety, efficiency, and compliance with OFGEM standards.

Working pattern: Monday to Friday, working 8.5-hour shifts (excluding meal breaks) between 08:00 and 20:00. During peak periods, you will be required to work approximately one in four Saturdays, with a weekday rest day provided in return.

In this role you will
- Deliver first-class customer service to internal and external customers; by overseeing the activities of all field-based staff to ensure they comply with field procedures
- Liaise with field-based staff and Emergency Site Managers regarding the scheduling and dispatching of work to ensure safety, customer satisfaction and efficiency are delivered
- Operate within business continuity procedures, to assist and support the Dispatch Team Leader throughout and after BCM events
- Communicate effectively with all customers including field-based personnel, and Site Managers
- Work within, and promote the philosophy of safe team working, innovative thinking and putting the customer first

We are looking for
- Flexibility to work alternating shifts, including weekends, bank holidays, and evenings
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, customer-facing environment
- Strong Microsoft Office skills and quick adaptability to new systems
- Excellent communication, prioritisation, and decision-making skills
- A collaborative team player with a focus on safety and service

Why join NGN?
- Salary from £29,286 per annum
- Up to 5% Bonus per annum
- 25 days of annual leave, plus recognised bank holidays and 2 additional half-days over the Christmas period
- Occupational sick pay available after the first 2 calendar days of statutory sick pay
- Generous stakeholder pension scheme, doubling your contribution, up to 10%
- Flexible benefits and salary sacrifice options, including discounts on UK attractions, gym memberships, restaurants, experience days, plus access to a virtual GP service
- Family-friendly policies, including up to 6 weeks of paternity leave and 6 months of full pay for maternity leave (for eligible employees), plus shared parental leave and more

About NGN

We deliver gas to 2.9 million homes and businesses across the North East, Northern Cumbria, and much of Yorkshire, through a network of over 37,000km of underground pipes. Serving both major cities and rural communities, we are committed to safety, reliability, and innovation. Our values Trailblazing, Empowered, Heartfelt, Community Focused, Intellectually Curious, and Happy, shape everything we do. We are proud to champion equality, diversity, and inclusion, and actively support initiatives alongside our Colleague Communities (LGBTQ/Women s/Roots&Resonance/Parents&Carers/AbilityMatters) to ensure we reflect and uplift the communities we serve.

Next Steps Simply click Apply and upload your CV, making sure to highlight how your skills and experience align with the role. We aim to contact all applicants within one week of the closing date, with interviews expected to take place end of October. If you require any adjustments during the recruitment process, please contact our Recruitment Team at (url removed)

title: Procurement Assistant
description:
We're recruiting for a Procurement Assistant to join an established and expanding procurement team based in Sunderland.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone at the beginning of their career who wants to gain hands-on experience, develop new skills and work towards a professional procurement qualification.

You'll be joining a supportive, collaborative and employee-owned business where your contribution is valued, your ideas are welcomed and there are genuine opportunities to progress.

Whether you're a school or college leaver, a recent graduate or someone looking to move into procurement from another industry, we'd love to hear from you.

The Role

Working alongside experienced procurement professionals, you'll support a variety of procurement and sourcing activities across goods, services, works and technology.

You'll gain exposure to the full procurement process, working with clients, suppliers and internal teams to ensure requirements are delivered efficiently and professionally.

This is a varied role where no two days will be the same, offering plenty of opportunities to learn, take responsibility and develop your commercial understanding.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Supporting the procurement team with day-to-day sourcing and purchasing activities.
- Helping clients identify suitable suppliers and service providers.
- Assisting with procurement processes, from initial requirements through to supplier selection.
- Communicating with clients and suppliers, responding to queries and providing updates.
- Supporting the onboarding of new suppliers and maintaining accurate supplier information.
- Carrying out basic research, data analysis and reporting.
- Preparing and maintaining procurement documentation and records.
- Monitoring shared inboxes and responding to enquiries.
- Supporting the team with meetings, administration and project coordination.
- Working with colleagues to identify opportunities to improve processes and service delivery.

About You

We're not necessarily looking for someone with previous procurement experience. What's more important is your attitude, willingness to learn and ability to communicate confidently with others.

You'll be someone who enjoys being busy, takes pride in doing a good job and is happy to take responsibility for your own workload.

Ideally, you'll have:
- GCSEs (or equivalent) in Maths and English.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Confidence communicating with people at different levels.
- A good understanding of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Outlook and Teams.
- The ability to prioritise tasks and manage your time effectively.
- Good numerical and analytical skills.
- A proactive, positive attitude and a willingness to learn.
- The ability to work independently while contributing to a wider team.

Previous office, administration, customer service or purchasing experience would be an advantage, but is not essential.

title: Site Administrator
description:
Freelance Site Administrator

Location: Sunderland
Sector: Social Housing / Repairs & Maintenance
Contract: Freelance
Duration: 5 months +
Rate: Competitive, dependent on experience

We are currently recruiting for a Freelance Site Administrator to join a well-established social housing contractor based in Sunderland.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced Site Administrator to support the delivery of social housing works, working closely with the site and operational teams to ensure projects are administered efficiently and effectively.

The Role

As Site Administrator, you will provide day-to-day administrative support to the project team, helping to ensure all site documentation, records and communications are kept up to date.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Providing general administrative support to the Site and Project Managers.
- Maintaining accurate project and site records.
- Managing and updating spreadsheets, databases and project documentation.
- Assisting with timesheets, labour records and subcontractor information.
- Raising and processing purchase orders and invoices where required.
- Maintaining health & safety and compliance documentation.
- Assisting with document control and filing.
- Liaising with operatives, subcontractors, clients and internal teams.
- Supporting the team with general project administration and reporting.
- Ensuring information is recorded accurately and issued within required timescales.

About You

The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Previous experience working as a Site Administrator / Project Administrator / Document Controller within construction.
- Experience within social housing, repairs & maintenance or planned works would be advantageous.
- Strong administration and organisational skills.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel and Word.
- The ability to manage multiple tasks and work to deadlines.
- Strong communication skills and a professional approach.
- Previous experience working within a busy construction/site environment.

description: There are so many reasons to join our team at Sunderland Specialist Eye Hospital. Aside from our fantastic staff, we have lots of exciting things going on. We have recently moved into our new Eye Hospital in Sunderland. The new hospital means Sunderland will remain home to the regions only dedicated standalone eye hospital. It will strengthen our excellent reputation across the NHS, both regionally and nationally as a centre of excellence for ophthalmology care. We also never stay still when it comes to discovering new and better treatments. As one of the few specialist eye hospitals in the country, research and using developing technology is a key part of our work. We encourage innovation and research in everything we do. There is always something to get involved in. If you share our vision for ' excellence in all that we do' , wed love you to join us! We invite you to submit an application for an ED Receptionist at Sunderland Eye Infirmary, working with multiple different staff groups, completing a variety of administration tasks and contributing to our fantastic service within our reception and medical records teams. This is an extremely busy and demanding role based in our Emergency Department Reception, working as part of a team of 3 ED receptionists covering a variety of shifts between 08:00 20:00 Monday-Sunday. To be responsible for registering attendances and updating patient demographic details in the patient administration system. To work on our NetCall system and manage our eye emergency telephone queue. To be first point of contact for all patients attending Sunderland Specialist Eye Hospital Emergency Department both face to face and on the phone. To support in the triage of patients. To complete scanning of documentation onto our patient systems. To work flexibily across other reception areas when required. Please note the Trust are not able to offer Skilled Worker Sponsorship for this role as it does not meet the UKVI threshold requirements. Applicants are requested to consider this when making their applic ation. Please visit Gov.UK for further information. PLEASE REFER TO THE ATTACHED JOB DESCRIPTION FOR FULL DUTIES OF THE ROLE. To provide a high quality reception service and care to patients attending the outpatients and Eye Emergency departments. To comply with the Trusts vision, values and behavioural compact.
